title.narrative: Second Program for Strengthening Governance for Enabling Service Delivery and Public Investment in Kenya

description.narrative: The proposed AF aims to deepen and accelerate reforms in priority areas critical to fiscal consolidation and public service delivery, building on the momentum of the parent Program, GESDeK II, whose development objective is to enhance revenue mobilization and deepen accountability and transparency in public finance management at the national government level.The AF is structured around four Results Areas: (i) Enhanced Revenue Mobilization, focusing on reducing VAT and Personal Income Tax (PIT) gaps through data analytics and expanding the eCitizen platform for non-tax revenue collection; (ii) Strengthened Public Spending Accountability and Transparency, targeting fiscal discipline through reduction of pending bills, implementation of a Treasury Single Account, improved cash management, and rollout of e-procurement; (iii) Improved Coordination of Priority Programs and Projects, through the establishment of a performance monitoring framework for government priority projects; and (iv) Enhanced External Audit and Oversight, strengthening the Office of the Auditor General's capacity for performance audits and introducing automated wealth declarations to support anti-corruption efforts. In addition, a new US$5 million Investment Project Financing (IPF) component will provide technical assistance and capacity building to support strategic planning and PFM IT architecture.The AF introduces new Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) to track progress across Results Areas, covering tax gap reduction, non-tax revenue growth, arrears clearance, cash management efficiency, e-procurement adoption, and timely verification of public officials' wealth declarations. The Program is expected to be approved in October 2026, with a proposed extension of the closing date by one year to December 31, 2029.
To enhance public sector efficiency, accountability, and transparency through improving revenue systems, spending controls, public sector effectiveness, and oversight.

title.narrative: Predictability, control, and transparency of budget execution are improved

baseline.value: (i) Most cash balances are consolidated on a monthly basis; (ii) Records are partly maintained for contracts including data on what has been procured, value of procurement, and who has been awarded contracts; (iii) The payroll is supported by full documentation for all changes made to personnel records each month and checked against the previous month's payroll data. Staff hiring and promotion is controlled by a list of approved staff positions.
